18/G.goal: Classify and explain the main tracking technologies used to determine user and device pose in VR and AR.
18/G.achieves: It gives the learner the hardware/software foundation needed to evaluate tracking choices and later implement an XR system with confidence.

18/O1.goal: Classify the main XR tracking technologies and explain how electromechanical, electromagnetic, and acoustic/ultrasonic trackers measure pose.
18/O1.achieves: It gives the learner a baseline for comparing sensor-based pose measurement options in VR and AR hardware.

18/O2.goal: Explain how vision-based XR tracking systems estimate pose from camera and depth sensor observations.
18/O2.achieves: It lets the learner compare inside-out and outside-in visual and depth approaches when selecting tracking for an XR application.

18/O3.goal: Explain how inertial tracking and GPS/RTK provide positional tracking in XR and where their limitations occur.
18/O3.achieves: It helps the learner understand self-contained and satellite-based position sources that complement camera-based tracking in system design.

18/O4.goal: Describe how XR tracking can be extended to full-body motion, gaze, and hybrid multi-sensor systems.
18/O4.achieves: It enables the learner to recognize how these methods support richer interaction and immersion in XR implementations.
